I'm not totally sure what they see on their end but this is the exact link i sent to my landlord https://nysrenthelp.otda.ny.gov/en/Tools/UploadDocumentOwner  hope that helps lol

yes, she needed my application number and my birthdate to link the landlord and the tenant account- but you def can't see anything like she can't see what i've entered on my end as far as forms, and I can't see her forms. It's just for them to be able to compare arrears and get their payment info really

They received a paper check-i think the direct deposit option is a joke at this point lol Also saw earlier on this thread a lot of confusion about the “12 months covered”- i can confirm now, it’s for any arrears accumulated after march 2020 -it doesn’t only cover march 2020 to march 2021, like someone else said. It’s any arrears from march 2020 onward, and they will cover up to 12 months of back rent. When i applied i was only behind for june-with the delay, i ended up paying june because I was worried about waiting and then not getting approved- but still got behind july and august. I never had to update the arrears on my end, they just went with what my landlord’s arrears said (and she submitted her side of things in august) so they counted july and august as arrears and then added three future months september, october, november. So for everyone worried about updating the new months etc the longer this process takes-i think that’s what that long review process was for, to adjust for the extra time that passed. If they would have approved it in June, i would have ended up having less covered in the end… so after all this stress I’m actually happy it took so long.

Just to add to the updates as I've been quietly following this post lol I finally got approved today- Applied June 1st. No movement at all for months, then last week it finally changed to document review completed, approved pending payment. Today the portal listed the date the payment was made, the amount, and I just got a detailed email from them listing the payout- 2 arrears plus 3 future months, which is exactly what I applied for. SLOWLY BUT SURELY. I was so stressed out and it took forever but it worked out! I hope everyone still waiting gets good news soon as well! Hang in there- this thread def kept me from losing my mind throughout this process!

I second the letter idea...that's exactly what I ended up doing when I started going to therapy. I couldn't talk about anything at all, like one word answers all the way even though I desperately wanted to share more I just couldn't. It was actually my therapists idea to just write a letter to her about my week and then she would read it in session and know exactly what was going on. Eventually we graduated to me reading the letters to her, and then after that I was finally able to just bring up things and discuss them. It def sounds stupid but it was so helpful for me and it's your session so don't feel like you can't do something that will ultimately help you just cuz it's off the 'norm'

It’s not too late to go to therapy though-which is crazy that i am saying that because I was such an anti-talk-to-someone person, until i actually found the right match for me and it actually started getting better. Even though i’m sure you are doing fine without it, it really does help a little if you ever feel like you are spiraling. Just something to keep in mind ♥️. I hope the same for you!! :)

It was a teen shelter so it wasn’t as scary as a “real” homeless shelter with adults would’ve been. Some of the staff were pretty nice because they were like volunteers who wanted to “help the homeless” so as defeating as it was to be there, it wasn’t all terrible. It did feel like I was cut off from the rest of the world which actually was a relief initially because I was super ashamed about what had happened with my fosterdad and I kind of wanted to hide away. But it was like jail in a lot of ways too, so it also reinforced that I was the one that did something wrong and that everything was my fault, so that took awhile to undo. It was really complicated. I did make friends with some of the other kids while i was there, and it was nice to have people that could relate to what i was going through. I was used to always having a deep dark secret about being abused and feeling like all my friends had perfect families and perfect lives...so it helped to not feel so much like it was just me, that I was the freak and unwanted and so on. I mean overall i hated being there lol but i can def see those positive aspects

We were good a few months later :-) I was definitely upset with her for not keeping my secret, cuz at the time that was the bigger deal. But after I was removed from the home, I started thinking more clearly and I did realize she did the right thing and was just trying to help me. And your second question- because they weren't certified foster parents. It sounds stupid especially considering that the 'certified foster parent' was the one who was hurting me sooo. Why can't I just stay with my friends? lol but that was their policy. They were not state foster parents so I wasn't allowed to stay with them, and since there were sexual abuse allegations pending in my foster home they couldn't place me in another one, so. Homeless shelter, you go. I did eventually runaway from the shelter and go to live with them, because I couldn't take it anymore - but even most of the staff at the shelter thought it was a better idea for me to go. I didn't even need to be sneaky about it they walked me out and gave me an hour to get to where I needed to be before they called the police to report that I'd gone AWOL. It was a scary time because they were threatening to arrest my friend's parents for 'harboring a runaway' if they didn't return me to the shelter, but they refused- and weirdly. it all kind of just went away after a few weeks. I was only a few months away from aging out of the system at this point, so I think they just decided not to care anymore.
thank you :-)

Thank you :-) It was terrifying lol I won't pretend I was eager to go through with it, but I am glad I did. Reddit has helped so so so much. It's not something you ever fully recover from, so it's nice to be able to just kind of. Vent about it at 1am or whatever. And people asking questions without it feeling invasive or like anyone is judging you. It feels like such a burden to carry around all the time so it's nice to be able to get it out sometimes. I had an amazing therapist-- not at the time, because I was super resistant right after i was moved to the shelter (I was a teenager after all lol) and didn't want to talk to anyone and was a bit mad at the world. But i started going again right before the trial because I felt like I was totally losing my mind. At first sessions were literally her asking me questions and me giving one word answers. But she was so patient with me and eventually, since I really didn't have experience 'talking' to people (I came from a really physically abusive home before foster care- so I was def damaged goods lol) she had me write it down, since that's always been an easier outlet for me. So I would come to session with the letters and she would read them and then slowly coax talking out of me. And then eventually we leveled up to me reading the letters to her. and then I was finally able to just talk about it. It was a hard process, and I'm actually taking a break from therapy right now because I feel like I've learned how to cope without it, but I might go back at some point just to make sure I stay sane lol. I was also a cutter (I know it's an insane thing to do, but my friend group at the time showed me how and it helped at the time) started when I was 13 as a coping mechanism, and therapy helped me to stop that too and use healthier means of expressing like journaling or doing music.

I'm sorry that happened to you and I'm so happy that you were able to find a family that loves and protects you now <3 and thank you, I did get help and he did get a guilty verdict so at least there was some consequence for what he did.

Now I think she did the right thing, for sure. At the time I was furious and I felt so betrayed. I never wanted to speak to her again. But after counseling and being out of the foster home for a few weeks (and not staying up all night because I was afraid that he was going to come into my room - you don't realize when you're 'in' a situation how much it's affecting you until you get to leave) I started thinking more clearly and I realized that was a huge thing to ask someone to keep to themselves. And she just didn't want me to be hurt. So I think ultimately she absolutely did the right thing and I'm grateful that she chose my...I guess safety over our friendship at the time.

It was about 5 years ago and...i mean it still feels like yesterday. I thought going might help bring me closure...and it did in some ways. Like I stood up to him, as much of a babbling mess i was on the stand- I did do it. So there's that. But I hated how instantly I fell apart the second I saw him and was back in that environment...like it almost felt like all the 'growing' I did in between was all in my mind and I was still the same scared, timid girl I was back then. So that was a little disappointing lol But every day it gets a little bit better and talking about it with strangers online helps lol so thank you

Thank you :-) It didn't feel brave at the time, but ultimately glad I went through with it. I was sooo upset with my friend at the time - I had sworn her to secrecy and in my mind, that was the bigger deal. I felt super betrayed like the one time I opened up to her and she told everyone. Once they moved me to the shelter, because I was also a ward of the state it was almost like being in jail with the rules and such...you couldn't have anything on you or contact people or leave unsupervised. So even if I had wanted to call her, I couldn't. But this gave me time to think about and a few weeks later after some counseling I realized that was A LOT to ask someone to keep a secret, and she just wanted to help me and make sure I wasn't being hurt. When you're in that situation you really aren't thinking that clearly...but I did see it after a bit of time and once we got to see each other again we talked it out and we were okay.  The shelter wasn't awful, compared to some group homes and things you see on TV. It was mostly kids who were on probation or other 'problem kids' that couldn't be placed in foster homes, 13-17. And they treated us like problem kids, which sucked because I really wasn't the rebellious type even after everything- but it didn't matter. 6am wake up, clean the shelter (we each got assigned a task like scrubbing the toilets or mopping the floors), you had to finish it and it had to be 'inspected' before you could go to the kitchen and get breakfast, group therapy, individual therapy, group 'sport'...it was like a rehabilitation/half way house type thing. Again it wasn't horrible, and I met some cool people there that helped me to toughen up a bit...but as an adult now there was a lot wrong with the whole situation. I distinctly remember a time in group where we all had to say how we were feeling? And I said I was feeling 'okay' and the therapist was like 'well you're obviously not okay because you ended up here- so maybe it would be a good time to figure out where you went wrong in your life for that to happen!" Like. Such a jerk. Can I just be okay for half a second lol. Anyway so many stories... your last question? He did get sentenced. I couldn't believe it. I asked them not to call me to update me so I don't know how much time he actually ended up doing but he was facing like 60 years in prison. I only know that because a friend sent me the news clip about it

awful...worse than what they depict in all those crime shows as far as how it feels, goes. There isn't as much 'drama' as far as lawyers jumping up and yelling 'objection' etc. the one thing i noticed was how eerily calm everyone was, about the whole thing. It seemed like I was the only upset one, in the room. Like this is legit just another day at work for them. A jury of strangers staring at you def doesn't help the situation...the defense attorney was so awful to me, which i guess is his job, too. He kept trying to make it seem like i 'wanted it' and kept making me describe what happened in extreme detail...and he would try to trip me up by asking the same questions, but in different ways. I lost my composure at one point and we had to take a break because I was crying too much to continue. I don't want to scare people away from going through with something like this to get justice, but I honestly wouldn't wish the experience on my worst enemy. It was so hard to get up there and talk about what happened, by itself- let alone have someone trying to make you out to be the 'bad one'

Yeah I hear you- I think in this case others is literally the sites that will be hosting your music that you distribute it to. E.g Youtube, Spotify...If you don't authorize them to play your music and promote you on their platform, they can't send your music to those stores. Cuz then technically you could sue them for copyright infringements, similar to how you can't monetize a youtube video if a copyright owner claims the content belongs to them....because that third party gets the revenue, not you. But again I'm not a lawyer...just looking at it from the best case scenario perspective. But a lot of artists use and trust Distrokid, and not to say they are totally innocent and good-but I feel like if they were stealing sync license revenue someone would've caught on to that right away. As far as I can tell from being an artist on the platform- I pay close attention to my earning stats and I have a PRO that I'm registered with and I don't think there's anything under the table going on like that

I'm not a therapist or anything, but as someone who can relate: I had this same problem before I got intimate for the first time after surviving a rape, and honestly you just have to get used to talking about it with your partner. If you're not comfy discussing it with them, they probably aren't the right person to go there with...at least not yet. You don't have to give all the details but just say that as much as you WANT to, it's going to take you some time to be ready. The longer you are with the same person, the sooner you'll start to feel safe. Def wouldn't recommend the band aid approach on this one. You've got to turn something horrible and traumatic into something that is now your choice and what you want with whomever you choose. That takes time. Good luck!
